{{< lifecycle-banner >}}

> **Model C — 15-facet multi-attribute (per [ADR-078](../../adr/adr-078-orgpath-attribute-schema-15-facet.qmd)).** OrgPath is now 10 named facet values across `extensionAttribute1`–`extensionAttribute10` per Entra principal (plus 5 reserved slots for tenant-declared facets). The Model A composite-hyphen path (`extensionAttribute1: ORG-FIN-AP-EAST`) is retired. See [codebook](codebook.qmd) for the slot-to-facet map, [dynamic groups](dynamic-groups.qmd) for the boolean-composition pattern, and the [drift walk-through](drift-walkthrough.qmd) for per-facet drift examples.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why this page exists

Most OrgPath confusion isn't about the canon — the canon is precise.
It's about which canonical artifact answers which operator question,
and which terminology means what. This FAQ collects the questions
that have actually been asked during assessment and migration work,
in the order they tend to come up, with the shortest accurate answer
and one or two pointers to the deeper doc.

If your question isn't here, that's a contribution opportunity — open
a PR adding it.
:::

## Storage and authority

### Where does OrgPath data actually live?

In three places at once, each playing a different role:

| Layer | Where | What it holds |
|-------|-------|---------------|
| **Vocabulary** | `src/uiao/canon/data/orgpath/codebook.yaml` (Git) | The 10 named facets and (per facet) an enumeration or typed pattern |
| **Assignment** | `extensionAttribute1`–`extensionAttribute10` on each Entra principal | The 10 actual facet values carried by every user/device |
| **Authority** | The HR system (Workday / SAP HR / HRIS) | The source of truth that drives the per-facet assignments |

See [Where OrgTree & OrgPath Data Lives](where-data-lives.qmd) for the
full Model C mental model.

### How is this different from just syncing an attribute with Entra Connect / Cloud Sync?

The sync tool is a **transport** — it reliably *moves* a value from
AD into an Entra `extensionAttribute` slot, and that's all it does. It
doesn't constrain what the value may be, notice when it stops matching
the org chart, or compose it into policy. OrgPath is the **governance**
layer one level up: the value that arrives is validated per facet
against the [codebook](codebook.qmd), checked continuously for [drift](#drift-detection),
and composed into dynamic groups, Administrative Units, and Conditional
Access by boolean facet predicates. Microsoft's sync gets the value
*into* Entra; UIAO makes it canonical, drift-resistant, and
policy-bearing. The control-plane/data-plane framing of that split — and
the dry-run reconcile loop (`uiao orgtree govern`) that closes it — is
the worked identity example in
[Active Governance](../platform/active-governance.qmd#worked-example-identity--sync-moves-the-attribute-orgpath-governs-it).

### Is OrgPath stored in a "registry"?

No — there is no separate registry database. The codebook is a YAML
file in Git; the 10 per-user facet values live on the Entra directory
object itself. The top-level `registry/` directory in this repo holds
*Governance OS adapter manifests* (pipeline sequencing, boundary
definitions). It is **not** the OrgPath store.

### Is it stored in Entra ID extension attributes? Are those attributes pre-defined?

Yes, across `extensionAttribute1`–`extensionAttribute10`. The 15 slots
themselves are **pre-defined by Microsoft** — `extensionAttribute1..15`
exist on every Entra tenant out of the box. UIAO doesn't create the
attributes; under ADR-078 it *claims* 10 of the 15 slots and binds
each to a named facet (Region, Department, Division, Role,
CostCenter, Classification, HireDate, TermDate, ClearanceLevel,
AccountType). Slots 11–14 are reserved for tenant-declared facets; slot 15 carries the derived canonical OrgPath (inheritance layer, ADR-127)
introduced via governed PR.

The *values* in the 10 slots are populated during migration and
maintained by HR-driven inbound provisioning. See
[ADR-063](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-063-orgpath-storage-slot-binding.md)
for the slot-binding rationale and [ADR-078](../../adr/adr-078-orgpath-attribute-schema-15-facet.qmd)
for the per-facet decomposition.

### Are the facet values pre-defined or built during AD assessment?

The *list of facets* (Region, Department, …) is pre-defined by
ADR-078. The *valid values inside each facet* (the per-facet
enumeration — which Departments exist, which Regions, which
ClearanceLevels, etc.) is built during assessment and shipped as
`codebook.yaml`. The *Microsoft attribute slots* that carry them are
pre-existing in every tenant. So: slots are pre-defined, facet
structure is canonical, per-facet enumerations are
assessment-defined, runtime values are migration-time + ongoing HR
provisioning.

### Who decides what facet values a given user has?

The HR system. The canon's operating rule is: *"HR system is the
authoritative source — IT never manually edits any of the 10 OrgPath
facet values."* Any IT-originated write to `extensionAttribute1`–`10`
is itself a drift event under the provenance rules in
[UIAO_163](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/UIAO_163_Drift_Detection_Engine_Specification.md).

### What if HR is wrong?

The drift engine still detects the disagreement between HR and Entra
and flags it as **Value Drift** (P2) on whichever specific facet
disagrees — Department, Region, ClearanceLevel, etc. When the HR
source is trusted as authoritative, Value Drift on principals can be
remediated by writing the HR value back to the specific slot. When HR
is suspected of being stale, the finding is escalated for human
review rather than auto-applied — see the
[Drift Detection Walk-through](drift-walkthrough.qmd) for the full
per-facet finding payload and severity ladder.

### What about contractors / non-HR-managed users?

If the principal isn't represented in the authoritative HR system,
they need an alternate source of authority documented in the
governance steward log. The most common pattern is a separate
contractor-management system that writes to a dedicated HR-equivalent
feed; the codebook itself doesn't care about the source, only that
*some* authoritative system owns the 10 facet values per principal.
The `Classification` facet (`extensionAttribute6`) explicitly carries
`Contractor` / `Intern` / `Vendor` / etc. to make the distinction
queryable.

### Is physical location (duty station) an OrgPath facet?

No — and deliberately so. Physical place is a **second addressing
dimension** called [LocPath](locpath.qmd), governed symmetrically to
OrgPath but kept apart per
[ADR-102](../../adr/adr-102-locpath-location-addressing.qmd): it claims
no `extensionAttribute` slot, and the OrgPath `Region` facet
(organizational reporting region) is *not* geography. Identities carry
both an OrgPath and a Primary LocPath, and governance rules can
predicate on the **matrix** of the two — e.g., *Finance-department
identities whose assigned place is not under the HQ campus*. The HR
system stays the single upstream authority for both placements
(ADR-088, extended to place by ADR-102 §D3).

## The codebook

### Where do new facet *values* come from?

A pull request adds a new entry to the relevant facet's `enumeration`
in `src/uiao/canon/data/orgpath/codebook.yaml`. The PR follows the
canonical Contributor Workflow
([UIAO_172](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/UIAO_172_Canonical_Contributor_Workflow.md))
— CI validates the JSON Schema, the Python loader's slot-uniqueness
invariant runs, reviewers approve; the codebook is signed and merged.

### Where do new *facets* come from?

If you need a facet not in the 10 named slots, declare it against one
of the 5 reserved slots (`extensionAttribute11`–`15`) via a governed
PR. Per ADR-078, verify the slot's current value is null tenant-wide
before promoting. Adding an entirely new facet beyond the reserved
slots requires a superseding ADR.

### Can I rebind a facet to a different slot?

No, not as a per-tenant override. The slot-to-facet mapping is
canonical (`Region` → `extensionAttribute1`, `Department` →
`extensionAttribute2`, etc.). Changing the binding across the canon
requires a superseding ADR. If a tenant's `extensionAttribute1` is
already in use for a non-OrgPath purpose, follow the
[ADR-063 §3](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-063-orgpath-storage-slot-binding.md)
rebind procedure to vacate the slot — never override the canonical
mapping.

### What does "slot uniqueness invariant" mean?

Each `extensionAttribute*` slot can be claimed by **exactly one**
facet. The Python loader rejects any codebook that declares two
facets binding the same slot — that's a **Slot Drift** (P1) finding.
JSON Schema can't express cross-property uniqueness, so the loader's
`_validate_integrity` step is the enforcement point.

### Are deprecated facet *values* ever cleaned up automatically?

No. A facet enumeration value marked `status: deprecated` with a
`replaced_by` successor triggers **Phantom Drift** (P3) for any
principal still carrying it; the engine auto-reassigns those
principals to the successor (when `auto_remediate=true` for that
facet). The deprecated enumeration entry itself is retained for audit
history — never deleted automatically — and is removed only via a
governed PR.

### What about facet values with zero matching principals?

Those are **Orphan Drift** (P3) — flagged for governance review but
never auto-deleted. The enumeration entry might be temporarily empty
during a reorganization, or might represent a structural placeholder
the org wants to retain. The operator decides.

### What about typed facets like HireDate and TermDate?

Two of the 10 named facets are typed rather than enumerated, because
dates aren't enumerable. `HireDate` (`extensionAttribute7`) and
`TermDate` (`extensionAttribute8`) validate against
`value_pattern: "^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$"` (ISO 8601). `TermDate`
additionally allows the empty string (`allow_empty: true`) — empty
TermDate means "still active." A value that fails the pattern is
**Format Drift** (P1).

## Devices, Azure resources, and service principals

### Is OrgPath stored on devices the same way as users?

Yes — the same 10-facet pattern, on the same `extensionAttribute*`
surface. Entra-joined client devices carry the 10 facet values in
`device.onPremisesExtensionAttributes.extensionAttribute1`–`10`,
exactly like users. Azure Arc servers (and other ARM-managed
resources tagged for governance) use the **equivalent 10 ARM tags**
on the resource instead, because that's the addressable surface for
`Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines`. See
[Where Data Lives — Devices and Azure](where-data-lives-devices-and-azure.qmd).

### What if a device is both Entra-joined and Arc-enrolled?

It carries the same 10 facet values in *both* surfaces and the canon
treats per-facet equality between them as a required invariant.
**Runtime cross-surface enforcement is deferred** — today, equality
is achieved at write time by the per-facet device-plane writer
(scheduled rebuild in ADR-078 Phase 5; the prior single-string
`EntraDeviceOrgPathAdapter` was retired in Phase 1), not by a runtime
drift-engine equality check. A future ADR will introduce that runtime
check.

### Are service principals / managed identities in scope?

Per [ADR-063](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-063-orgpath-storage-slot-binding.md),
yes — the canonical surface is `servicePrincipal.extensionAttribute1`–`10`
under the same 10-facet model. However, the drift engine v1 reads
only the user and device surfaces; SP consumption is deferred.

### Why not just use an Intune scope tag for devices?

Intune scope tags *derive* from the device's 10 facet values — they
aren't an independent storage location. Putting OrgPath data directly
into a scope tag would create two sources of truth and break the
per-facet agreement rule with the Entra device's
`extensionAttribute*` surface. See
[Customer narrative ch. 5 — OrgPath and Intune](../orgpath-narrative/Book_05.qmd)
for the device-lifecycle treatment.

## Drift detection

### What are the five drift categories?

Per Model C, all five operate per-facet (a finding names the specific
slot and facet that disagrees):

| Category | What broke | Severity | Auto-fix? |
|----------|-----------|----------|-----------|
| **Format** | A typed facet's value fails its `value_pattern` regex | P1 | No |
| **Value** | An enumerated facet's value is not in the facet's `enumeration` | P2 | Sometimes (HR write-back when authoritative) |
| **Slot** | A facet's `attribute:` was remapped without ADR (or two facets bind the same slot) | P1 | No — codebook integrity issue |
| **Orphan** | A facet enumeration value has zero matching principals | P3 | Flag only |
| **Phantom** | A principal carries a deprecated enumeration value | P3 | Reassign (when `replaced_by` is set) |

The [Drift Walk-through](drift-walkthrough.qmd) has concrete per-facet
examples and sample `DriftFinding` JSON for each category.

### What does per-facet drift detection mean in practice?

A principal whose `Region` is valid but whose `Department` is unknown
produces **one** finding — for the `Department` slot only. The
`Region` slot passes independently. Composite-string parsing is gone;
each of the 10 slots validates as its own facet, so refactoring one
facet's enumeration never invalidates the others.

### How often does the drift engine run?

The cadence is defined by the deployment, not the canon — typical
production cadences are nightly for full per-facet population scans
and on-demand via CLI for targeted re-checks after remediation. The
engine itself is stateless between runs; every scan is a fresh
per-facet snapshot.

### Can I dry-run the drift engine?

Yes — `DriftScanReport` carries a `dry_run` boolean. With
`dry_run=true` the engine emits findings but applies no remediation;
this is the default for new tenants and for CI gates. (The per-facet
runtime engine is scheduled for rebuild in ADR-078 Phase 5; the
behavioral contract above is preserved from UIAO_163 v1.)

## Tenant-specific concerns

### My tenant already uses `extensionAttribute1` for something else. What do I do?

Don't write over it. Follow the rebind procedure in
[ADR-063 §3](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/adr/adr-063-orgpath-storage-slot-binding.md):
snapshot the prior values to the Evidence Fabric, relocate the
inherited use to a slot UIAO does not claim (e.g.,
`extensionAttribute11`–`15` are reserved for tenant-declared facets,
but you must not co-occupy with a UIAO-planned facet), verify
cutover, *then* enable per-facet OrgPath writes. Tenants where the
slot cannot be vacated are blocked from the modernization pipeline by
design — that decision sits with the governance steward, not the
deploying operator.

### Can I just pick different slots in my tenant?

No. The 10 slot-to-facet bindings are not per-tenant configuration
knobs. Attempting to retarget in code (e.g., editing the facet's
`attribute:` field in `codebook.yaml`) is a canon violation and fails
CI under
[UIAO_172](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/UIAO_172_Canonical_Contributor_Workflow.md)
— the Python loader will catch the slot-uniqueness violation and the
schema check will reject inconsistent bindings.

### Can I add my own facet?

Yes — but only against one of the 5 reserved slots
(`extensionAttribute11`–`15`), declared via a governed PR that
specifies the facet name, kind (enumerated or typed), and either an
enumeration or a typed validation pattern. Verify the slot's current
value is null tenant-wide before promoting (per ADR-078 reserved-slot
discipline).

## Diagrams and rendering

### Do we have images for this?

The image *prompts* and *registry entries* are in the repo
(UIAO-FIG-012 OrgPath storage, UIAO-FIG-013 drift engine loop,
UIAO-FIG-014 device/Azure routing). The *rendered PNGs* are produced
on demand by the Gemini-based image pipeline. The status of a given
figure is recorded in
[`src/uiao/canon/image-registry.yaml`](https://github.com/WhalerMike/uiao/blob/main/src/uiao/canon/image-registry.yaml)
under `status:` — `draft` means the prompt exists but the PNG hasn't
been generated yet; `current` means it's rendered and approved.

### How do I render a figure?

Two paths, both documented in the
[Image Pipeline & Registry Guide](../../academy/image-pipeline-guide.qmd):

- **Local:** `export GEMINI_API_KEY=…` then
  `python scripts/generate_images.py`.
- **GitHub Actions:** Dispatch the `image-gen.yml` workflow with
  `commit_back: true` for canon figures so `file_sha256` is
  backfilled atomically with the PNG landing.

### How do I find if a figure I need already exists?

Use the registry search CLI:

```bash
python scripts/tools/image_registry_search.py "your topic"
```

Or filter by audience / document-type / visual-style. The CLI ranks
by weighted field match with `reuse_score` as the tiebreaker, so the
most-reused canonical image for a subject surfaces first. Prefer
`[IMAGE-REF: UIAO-FIG-NNN]` reuse over a fresh `[IMAGE-NN: …]` prompt
— cheaper to render, visually consistent, drift-tracked.
